summary: Recorded the execution-backed account of the removed-singleton-leader question. CheckRun bc8372740399467686bed25385e51001 (fixed experiment 8f8a7578765146509956132f0183a8c3-experiment, version 2) parsed six events with no loss and resolved every comparison: four hold and the witness is violated. Change in the account: the question is no longer empirically undecided - parsed index 1 shows the node whose removal the application applied still StateLeader at term 1 with config voters=(2), singleton true and is_voter false; index 2 shows the actual leader at term 2 with committed index 4 while the removed leader sits at 2; index 3 is the violated witness, the removed leader answering the read with read_index 2 - below the entry the actual leader had already committed - with heartbeats_emitted 0, no messages, no pending or unconfirmed reads, i.e. produced wholly by the size shortcut; index 4 is the control, the same request on the actual leader returning index 4; index 5 shows a second request answered with the same stale index after three heartbeat intervals with no replies. Conclusion violated with defect_claim asserted, scoped as a stale, unconfirmed ReadIndex answer from a node whose own configuration proves it is not the voter, with the explicit caveats that the shortcut is sound when the single voter is the local node, that the client's read-from-the-leader premise is what makes it reachable, and that the window depends on the default StepDownOnRemoval=false with CheckQuorum and PreVote off; knowledge revisions 1 are cited. Incomplete: the forwarded MsgReadIndexResp form of the same shortcut is unmeasured, no state machine was run so the stale served value is a contract consequence rather than a measured read, and both questions remain open for further sourced leads.
